findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: Write endpoints (POST /orders, DELETE /orders/{id}, POST /orders/{id}/refund, POST /orders/{id}/cancel) have no idempotency key support. The code explicitly documents: 'No Idempotency-Key => a retry double-refunds.'
findings.gap: No idempotency middleware, no Idempotency-Key header support, no unique constraint enforcement on business keys for write operations.
findings.recommendation: Add Idempotency-Key header support to all state-mutating endpoints using a Fastify plugin that stores idempotency keys in PostgreSQL.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no idempotency keys on write endpoints.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The service exposes POST/DELETE write endpoints that execute real money movement (refund) and irreversible deletions. An agent retrying a timed-out call will double-refund or duplicate operations.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add Idempotency-Key header support to POST /orders, POST /orders/{id}/refund, and POST /orders/{id}/cancel.
blocker_remediation.target_state: All state-mutating endpoints accept and enforce an Idempotency-Key header; duplicate requests return cached response.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: The ECS task definition configures CloudWatch logging (awslogs driver) but the application does not log the authenticated principal (JWT subject/roles) for write operations. No CloudTrail configuration exists. CloudWatch Logs are not configured with immutability controls.
findings.gap: Authenticated principal not logged per write operation. No immutable/tamper-evident log storage. No CloudTrail.
findings.recommendation: Attach JWT sub claim to Fastify request context in auth middleware; configure structured logging to include principal. Export logs to S3 with Object Lock.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no audit logging of authenticated principal per write operation.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Write-enabled agents executing DELETE, refund, and cancel operations must have full audit attribution. The system logs to CloudWatch but does not include the JWT principal in log entries.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Attach JWT sub claim to Fastify log context; configure structured logging with principal on every request.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every write operation logs the authenticated principal to an immutable store (S3 with Object Lock or CloudTrail with log file validation).

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: Multi-step write operations (refund: update DB + call payment; cancel: update DB + call warehouse) perform sequential mutations without compensation logic. If downstream call fails after DB update, system is left in inconsistent state.
findings.gap: No saga pattern, no compensating transactions, no atomic multi-step execution.
findings.recommendation: Wrap multi-step operations in database transactions; commit only after downstream success, or implement compensating actions.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND multi-step write operations have no compensation logic.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The refund method updates order status then calls warehouse.issueRefund(); cancel updates status then calls warehouse.recallDispatch(). If downstream fails after DB commit, the order is left in an inconsistent state with no rollback mechanism.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Wrap refund and cancel in database transactions; only commit after downstream call succeeds.
blocker_remediation.target_state: All multi-step write operations either succeed atomically or roll back/compensate.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The system stores customer-identifiable data (customerId, order transaction amounts) in PostgreSQL. No data residency documentation, sovereignty policies, or cross-boundary transfer restrictions exist.
findings.gap: No data residency policy documented. No boundary controls restricting data transmission to specific regions or jurisdictions.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements for customer order data. Identify applicable regulations based on customer base geography. Add data classification tags to infrastructure resources.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND customer-identifiable data stored without explicit residency controls.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q2 fired because the system stores customer-identifiable data (customerId, totalCents) with no documented residency policy or boundary controls. An agent could transmit this data to an LLM in a different jurisdiction without restriction.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: JWT tokens verified with issuer/audience validation but no on-behalf-of flow exists. No distinction between agent acting under own identity vs. on behalf of a user.
findings.gap: No identity propagation through service calls. No actor/user distinction.
findings.recommendation: Implement separate OAuth2 client credentials for agent identities with distinct JWT claims (actor_type, on_behalf_of).

compensating_controls: Scope agent permissions to read-only initially; require agent requests to include a user context header
Enforce separate JWT audiences for agent vs human callers

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: No mechanism for immediate agent identity suspension. JWT-only auth with no token denylist or per-agent disable mechanism.
findings.gap: Cannot suspend a specific agent identity without affecting all tokens signed by the same key.
findings.recommendation: Add a token denylist (Redis or DynamoDB) checked in auth middleware, or implement OAuth2 token introspection.

compensating_controls: Use short-lived JWTs (< 5 minutes)
Add a token denylist check for emergency revocation

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No optimistic locking, version fields, ETags, or SELECT FOR UPDATE patterns. Multiple concurrent agent instances could silently overwrite each other's changes.
findings.gap: No concurrency controls on write operations. Race conditions possible.
findings.recommendation: Add a version column to the orders table and implement optimistic locking in UPDATE queries.

compensating_controls: Limit agent concurrency to single instance per order
Add optimistic locking via version column

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: External calls to WarehouseClient (issueRefund, recallDispatch) have no circuit breaker, retry logic, or timeout configuration.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns on external dependency calls. Failures cascade directly.
findings.recommendation: Wrap WarehouseClient calls with circuit breaker (opossum) and configure timeouts with exponential backoff.

compensating_controls: Set HTTP client timeouts on warehouse client
Implement circuit breaker on external calls

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting configured at any layer. No rate limiting middleware, no API Gateway throttling, no WAF rate rules. SAFETY.md explicitly identifies this gap.
findings.gap: No rate limiting. An agent loop could overwhelm the service at machine speed.
findings.recommendation: Add @fastify/rate-limit plugin and/or API Gateway throttling configuration.

compensating_controls: Add fastify-rate-limit middleware
Deploy API Gateway with throttling

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No configurable transaction limits. No caps on refund amounts, delete operations, or bulk operation sizes per session or caller.
findings.gap: No per-caller business transaction limits. Unlimited refunds/deletes possible.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent-identity transaction limits: max refund per hour, max deletions per day.

compensating_controls: Add per-token daily refund cap
Implement max-deletions-per-session counter

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No draft or pending state for agent-proposed writes. All write operations commit immediately. Order status values (placed, shipped, cancelled, refunded) have no PENDING_REVIEW or PROPOSED state.
findings.gap: No mechanism for agent to propose changes for human review before execution.
findings.recommendation: Add pending status values (pending_refund, pending_cancel, pending_delete) for agent-initiated destructive operations.

compensating_controls: Add PENDING_APPROVAL status for destructive operations
Route agent requests through approval queue at orchestration layer

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No operations require human approval. DELETE, refund, and cancel endpoints execute immediately upon receiving a valid authenticated request.
findings.gap: No configurable approval gates on high-risk operations.
findings.recommendation: Add per-operation approval configuration with threshold-based gates (e.g., refund > $100 requires approval).

compensating_controls: Route agent requests through approval service at orchestration layer
Add requires_approval config flag per operation

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A: System stores customer-identifiable data. Stage B: B1 CLEAR (no credentials exposed in API), B2 RISK-SAFETY (single orders:read scope grants access to all order data for all customers — no data-domain differentiation), B3 INFO (no formal classification metadata).
findings.gap: B2: No access control differentiation between sensitive and non-sensitive data domains.
findings.recommendation: Introduce granular OAuth scopes differentiating metadata from financial data. Implement row-level security for customer segmentation.

compensating_controls: Implement OAuth scopes separating data domains
Add row-level filtering for agent customer segments

b1.reasoning: API responses return business-operational fields (id, customerId, status, totalCents) needed for order management. No passwords, card numbers, or credentials exposed.

b2.reasoning: Single orders:read scope grants access to all order data for all customers. No granular scope separation between financial data and metadata.

b3.reasoning: No formal data classification tags, no PII detection tooling, no field-level sensitivity annotations.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: CloudWatch logging configured with no PII masking middleware. CustomerId and order data could appear in error logs. No log scrubbing, no CloudWatch data protection policies.
findings.gap: No PII redaction in logging pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Add Fastify logger serializer that redacts PII fields. Consider CloudWatch Log data protection policies.

compensating_controls: Add Fastify serializer hooks that redact sensitive fields
Configure CloudWatch Log subscription filter for PII detection

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses include structured JSON with code and message fields but lack a retryable indicator or error category.
findings.gap: No retryable boolean or error category. Agent cannot determine retry strategy from response body.
findings.recommendation: Extend error schema to include retryable boolean and error category.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration. No docker-compose, no environment-specific IaC, no seed data.
findings.gap: No safe environment for agent testing without risk to live systems.
findings.recommendation: Create docker-compose.yml with PostgreSQL and seed data for local agent testing.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation libraries. Request bodies cast with TypeScript 'as' assertions without runtime validation. No structured validation error responses.
findings.gap: No runtime input validation at API boundary. Malformed payloads accepted without rejection.
findings.recommendation: Add @sinclair/typebox or zod for runtime validation with Fastify schema support.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: No temporal fields (created_at, updated_at) in Order entity. No freshness headers in API responses.
findings.gap: No timestamps. Agents cannot determine data currency.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at/updated_at columns and Last-Modified response headers.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: OpenAPI spec has version 2.1.0 but no runtime versioning enforcement, no breaking change detection tools, and no contract tests.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy enforced at runtime. No breaking change detection in CI.
findings.recommendation: Add URL prefix versioning and integrate oasdiff in CI for breaking change detection.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: CloudWatch logging configured but no distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, X-Ray), no trace ID propagation, and no correlation IDs.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing. No correlation IDs linking log entries for a single request.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK or AWS X-Ray instrumentation with request correlation IDs.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting thresholds configured. No CloudWatch Alarms in IaC. Error rate and latency degradation would not trigger automated alerts.
findings.gap: No automated alerting for error rates or latency on agent-facing APIs.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch Alarms for ALB 5xx rate and p99 latency to CloudFormation template.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance
findings.description: IaC exists (CloudFormation in infra/ecs.yaml) but no peer review enforcement or drift detection configured.
findings.gap: IaC present but no governance controls beyond definition.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS Config drift detection and PR review requirements for infra/ changes.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration in repository. Build/test/lint scripts exist in package.json but no automation runs them.
findings.gap: No CI/CD pipeline. No automated contract testing or breaking change detection.
findings.recommendation: Add CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI) that runs build, test, lint, and OpenAPI validation on PRs.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: Vitest configured as test framework but no test files exist in repository. Zero API test coverage.
findings.gap: No test files. No API tests validating endpoint behavior.
findings.recommendation: Write Vitest integration tests for all endpoints covering valid/invalid inputs, auth failures, and error responses.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No KMS encryption configuration for data store. RDS not provisioned in this CloudFormation template. Encryption status of external database unknown.
findings.gap: Encryption at rest status unknown for PostgreSQL database.
findings.recommendation: Document or configure encryption for the external RDS instance (StorageEncrypted: true with KMS key).

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: All responses are JSON (Fastify default content-type application/json). Well-suited for LLM consumption.
findings.gap: None — JSON is optimal for agent tool integration.
findings.recommendation: No action needed.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: State changes (order status transitions) occur but no events emitted. No SNS/SQS/EventBridge integration.
findings.gap: No event emission. Agents must poll to detect state changes.
findings.recommendation: Add EventBridge events for order status transitions.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limits documented in OpenAPI spec. No X-RateLimit-Remaining or Retry-After headers returned.
findings.gap: No rate limit documentation or headers for agent self-throttling.
findings.recommendation: Once rate limiting is implemented, document limits in OpenAPI spec and return rate limit headers.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality metrics, profiling, or completeness monitoring exist for the orders data.
findings.gap: No data quality visibility for agents.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding data quality checks (orphaned orders, incomplete records) as service matures.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer. Schema documented implicitly via TypeScript interface and OpenAPI spec only.
findings.gap: No formal data catalog describing what data the system holds.
findings.recommendation: Add lightweight data dictionary in repository documentation.

findings.title: Business Outcome Metrics
findings.description: No custom business outcome metrics published. Only infrastructure-level CloudWatch logging configured.
findings.gap: No business-level signal for agent interaction outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch custom metrics for orders_created, orders_refunded, cancellation rates.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: REST API exposed via Fastify with OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec at openapi/orders.yaml documenting all endpoints.

evaluations.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
evaluations.reason: OpenAPI 3.0.3 specification exists at openapi/orders.yaml with all endpoints, operation IDs, and security scheme defined.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no evidence of operations exceeding 30 seconds or long-running workflows.

evaluations.title: Machine Identity Authentication
evaluations.reason: JWT RS256 auth with remote JWKS, issuer/audience verification, and role claims. Supports machine identity via OAuth2 client credentials flow.

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions
evaluations.reason: Role-based authorization with distinct scopes: orders:read for reads, orders:write for mutations. Supports least-privilege agent identities.

evaluations.title: Action-Level Authorization
evaluations.reason: Action-level enforcement: GET requires orders:read, POST/DELETE require orders:write. Agent can read without write access.

evaluations.title: Credential Management
evaluations.reason: Credentials managed via AWS Secrets Manager (DbSecret with auto-generated password, injected as ECS task secret). No hardcoded credentials.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: GET /orders/:id provides queryable current state (id, customerId, status, totalCents) for agent inspection before action.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no P0 priority assigned, not identified as critical path service.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — service has no list/query endpoints with potentially unbounded results (only single-item GET by ID).

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: All field names are semantically meaningful: customerId, totalCents, status, amountCents. No legacy abbreviations.

evaluations.title: Rollback Capability
evaluations.reason: ECS service configured with DeploymentCircuitBreaker: Enable: true, Rollback: true — automatic rollback on failed deployments.

items.summary: Resolve all BLOCKERs (idempotency, audit logging, compensation, data residency) and critical RISK-SAFETY findings (rate limiting, concurrency, HITL controls, PII redaction) to unblock agent deployment.
Address remaining RISK-SAFETY (identity propagation, transaction limits) and RISK-QUALITY findings (validation, observability, CI/CD, encryption) to enable controlled pilot.
Improve agent effectiveness with test coverage, event emission, business metrics, and documentation.

recommended_actions.action: Implement idempotency keys on all write endpoints
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents duplicate refunds and operations when agents retry on timeout — the highest-impact BLOCKER.

recommended_actions.action: Add audit logging with principal attribution and immutable storage
recommended_actions.rationale: Required for compliance and forensics when agents execute write operations.
Prevents inconsistent state when downstream calls fail after local DB commits.

recommended_actions.action: Document data residency policy and add boundary controls
recommended_actions.rationale: Customer-identifiable data needs explicit residency controls before agent transmission to LLMs.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy rate limiting and transaction caps
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents agent loops from overwhelming the service or executing unbounded operations.

recommended_actions.action: Add human-in-the-loop controls for irreversible operations
recommended_actions.rationale: DELETE, refund, and cancel operations need draft states and approval gates for agent safety.
